---
title: "repo"
toc: true
---

The `repo` subcommand is used to set up repositories.

## Commands

```
  repo readme
  repo devcontainer [--repo <owner>/<repo>@<branch>] [--build]
  repo action <action-name>
```

## `repo readme`

This command interacts with the user to scaffold a standardized `README.md` for a project repository.

When executed, it prompts for the following information:
- The project title.
- A brief description of what the repository does.
- The full names and email addresses of two primary contacts.

It then generates a `README.md` using the provided inputs.

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

The generated `README.md` follows a clean template containing sections for the title, purpose, contact details, links (e.g. data sources, publications), and further details (e.g. methods, timeline, team, data sources).

For example, the output might look like:

```markdown
# My Project Title

This repository handles data processing for the survey data.

## Contact

For more information, please contact:
- Jane Doe:
  - jane.doe@example.com
- John Smith:
  - john.smith@example.com

## Links

- [URLs to data sources (e.g. OneDrive), GitHub repositories, publications, etc.]

## Details

[Methods, timeline, team, data sources, software/tools, etc.]
```
:::

## `repo devcontainer`

This command copies a reference `.devcontainer` configuration into your current repository.

```bash
setupmjr repo devcontainer [--repo <owner>/<repo>@<branch>] [--build]
```

- `--repo`: Specifies the source repository and branch to copy the `.devcontainer` directory from (defaults to `MiguelRodo/comp@main`).
- `--build`: If provided, the command also installs the `prebuild-devcontainer.yml` workflow example from the latest published `MiguelRodo/actions` release.

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

The source archive is downloaded completely to a temporary file before extraction, so a timeout or interrupted HTTP body cannot feed a partial archive into `tar`. Repository and branch values are passed as command arguments rather than interpolated into a shell command. The optional prebuild workflow is fetched from an exact published actions release tag rather than mutable `main`.

setupmjr-owned HTTP downloads use a finite request timeout and report the request URL and HTTP status on failures such as `403 Forbidden`. Failed or incomplete file downloads are discarded rather than being left at their final destination path.
:::

## Install `repos`

Repository orchestration belongs to the standalone `repos` command. Install or update it with:

```bash
setupmjr install --repos
```

Then invoke `repos` directly. `setupmjr` no longer proxies `repos` commands. The release archive is staged in a temporary directory and is not extracted after a failed or incomplete download.

## `repo action`

This command installs a workflow example published by the canonical [`MiguelRodo/actions`](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/actions) repository:

```bash
setupmjr repo action <action-name>
```

`setupmjr` first resolves the latest published actions release, then downloads `examples/<action-name>.yml` from that exact release tag into `.github/workflows/`. It keeps no embedded workflow copies and does not fall back to mutable `actions/main`.

The available names are therefore the files present in the `examples` directory of the latest published actions release. For the current v3 release this includes `prebuild-devcontainer`, `publish-quarto-site`, and `version-release`. If a requested example is not published in that release, the command fails instead of installing a local or development copy.

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

Workflow downloads are staged in `.github/workflows/` and replace the final path only after the response completes successfully. Errors include the requested action name, resolved release tag, and HTTP status where available.
:::
